title: Relative strength
summary: Relative strength compares one market with another, or with an index, as a ratio of prices. A rising ratio means the first did better over that window.
unreliableWhen: Results depend on the start date chosen, leadership changes without warning, and markets with very different volatility are hard to compare. The first market can fall while showing relative strength.
goodExample: Stock A up 10% while its index is up 5%: the ratio rose about 4.8% over that window.
badExample: Reading a rising ratio as "A is going up", or confusing relative strength with RSI.
